passages.text: Home / Investor Corner / Expense Ratio Expense Ratio Under SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, Mutual Funds are permitted to charge certain operating expenses for managing a mutual fund scheme – such as sales & marketing / advertising expenses, administrative expenses, transaction costs, investment management fees, registrar fees, custodian fees, audit fees – as a percentage of the fund’s daily net assets. All such costs for running and managing a mutual fund scheme are collectively referred to as ‘Total Expense Ratio’ (TER) The TER is calculated as a percentage of the Scheme’s average Net Asset Value (NAV). The daily NAV of a mutual fund is disclosed after deducting the expenses. Currently, in India, the expense ratio is fungible, i.e., there is no limit on any particular type of allowed expense as long as the total expense ratio is within the prescribed limit. The regulatory limits of TER that can be incurred/charged to the fund by a Mutual Fund AMC have been specified under Regulation 52 of SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations. Effective from April 1, 2020 the TER limit has been revised as follows. In addition, mutual funds have been allowed to charge up to 30 bps more, if the new inflows from retail investors from beyond top 30 cities (B30) cities are at least (a) 30% of gross new inflows in the scheme or (b) 15% of the average assets under management (year to date) of the scheme, whichever is higher. This is essentially to encourage inflows into mutual funds from tier - 2 and tier - 3 cities. TER has a direct bearing on a scheme’s NAV – the lower the expense ratio of a scheme, the higher the NAV . Thus, TER is an important parameter while selecting a mutual fund scheme. passages.text: :: Securities Market Investment: Understanding the Riskometer | SEBI Investor :: Home Personal Finance and Investment Securities Market Investment Content Understanding the Riskometer Understanding the Riskometer Investing is an essential part of personal finance, but it comes with its fair share of risks. To help investors make informed decisions, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) introduced a tool called the Riskometer. This tool provides a clear and visual representation of the risk level associated with a particular mutual fund scheme, allowing investors to match their risk appetite with investment options. What is a Riskometer? The Riskometer is a risk-measuring tool used in the mutual fund industry to depict the risk level of a mutual fund scheme. It is mandatory for asset management companies to display the Riskometer on their schemes as per guidelines by SEBI. The Riskometer simplifies complex risk assessments, giving investors a snapshot of the potential risks involved in a fund, ranging from low to very high. How Does the Riskometer Work? The Riskometer classifies mutual fund schemes into five risk categories: Low Risk: Investments are considered safe, with minimal volatility. Ideal for conservative investors who prioritize capital protection.. Low to Moderate Risk: Slightly higher risk than low-risk funds but still relatively stable. Moderate Risk: Balanced risk level suitable for investors willing to take calculated risks. Moderately High Risk: Investments with significant exposure to market volatility. Potential for high returns but comes with higher risks. High Risk: Investment with higher risk than moderate. Potential for high return with high risk. Very High Risk: Highly volatile and risky investments, suitable for aggressive investors seeking substantial returns. Each level is color-coded to improve visual clarity for investors: Low Risk: Irish Green Low to Moderate Risk: Chartreuse Moderate Risk: Neon Yellow Moderately High Risk: Caramel High Risk: Dark Orange Very High Risk: Red The classification is based

Market volatility Credit risk and interest rate sensitivity. Benefits of the Riskometer Risk Assessment: The Riskometer helps investors gauge the risk level of a mutual fund scheme before investing. Decision Making: Investors can align their risk appetite with the right fund category. Transparency: It ensures that mutual funds are transparent about their risk levels, fostering trust. Simplification: The visual representation is easy to understand, making it accessible to novice investors. Enhanced Awareness: Investors become more aware of the risk-return trade-off. Informed Decisions: It helps investors choose funds that match their financial goals and risk tolerance. Standardized Tool: Being a regulatory mandate, it ensures consistency across all fund houses. Prevention of Mismatched Investments: Avoids scenarios where low-risk investors end up in high-risk schemes inadvertently. The risk levels are reviewed periodically and updated based on changing market conditions Fund houses must include the Riskometer in their fact sheets and promotional materials. It applies to all mutual fund categories, including equity, debt, and hybrid funds. It is required to adhere to SEBI guidelines, ensuring uniformity.
